problem: The sentence repeats itself: 'The most common set is the mel-frequency cepstral coefficient (MFCC); some syllabi call it the mel-frequency cepstral coefficient.' The second clause says exactly the same thing as the first, so the student gets no new information and may think a distinction is being made.
fix: State the expansion once and add a useful second clause, for example: 'The most common set is the mel-frequency cepstral coefficient (MFCC); the plural form, mel-frequency cepstral coefficients, is also written MFCCs.'

where: Section 3 table, GSM full rate row
problem: GSM full rate is labelled 'hybrid CELP'. GSM full rate (13 kbps) actually uses RPE-LTP, regular-pulse excitation with long-term prediction. It is a hybrid analysis-by-synthesis coder like CELP, but it has no excitation codebook, so calling it CELP contradicts the standard description.
fix: Change the Idea entry to 'hybrid (RPE-LTP, analysis-by-synthesis)' and keep CELP as the label for G.729 and similar codebook coders.

problem: The section introduces deltas and delta-deltas but the only formula shown is the cepstral-mean-normalisation one. The reader is told a delta is the slope of a coefficient over nearby frames but is never given the standard regression expression, so the 39-dimensional count cannot be reproduced from the text.
fix: Add the usual formula Δc<sub>t</sub> = (Σ<sub>k=1..K</sub> k(c<sub>t+k</sub> − c<sub>t−k</sub>)) / (2Σ<sub>k=1..K</sub> k²), with K about 2 frames, and say the delta-delta is the same regression applied to the deltas.
